name: Create a repository webhook
description: Create a repository webhook Repositories can have multiple webhooks installed. POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
context:
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
Repositories can have multiple webhooks installed. Each webhook should have a unique `config`. Multiple webhooks can share the same `config` as long as those webhooks do not have any `events` that overlap.
Required: owner (path) — The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.; repo (path) — The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.
Optional: body (body)

name: Delete a repository webhook
description: Delete a repository webhook Delete a webhook for an organization. DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}

name: Get a repository webhook
description: Get a repository webhook Returns a webhook configured in a repository. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}

name: Get a webhook configuration for a repository
description: Get a webhook configuration for a repository Returns the webhook configuration for a repository. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/config
context:
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/config
Returns the webhook configuration for a repository. To get more information about the webhook, including the `active` state and `events`, use "[Get a repository webhook](/rest/webhooks/repos#get-a-repository-webhook)." OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:repo_hook` or `repo` scope to use this endpoint.
Required: owner (path) — The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.; repo (path) — The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

name: Get a delivery for a repository webhook
description: Get a delivery for a repository webhook Returns a delivery for a webhook configured in a repository. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}

name: List deliveries for a repository webhook
description: List deliveries for a repository webhook Returns a list of webhook deliveries for a webhook configured in a repository. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries
context:
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries
Returns a list of webhook deliveries for a webhook configured in a repository.
Required: owner (path) — The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.; repo (path) — The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.
Optional: per_page (query) — The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."; cursor (query) — Used for pagination: the starting delivery from which the page of deliveries is fetched. Refer to the `link` header for the next and previous page cursors.; status (query) — Returns webhook deliveries filtered by delivery outcome classification based on `status_code` range. A `status` of `success` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 200-399 range (inclusive). A `status` of `failure` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 400-599 range (inclusive).

name: List repository webhooks
description: List repository webhooks Lists webhooks for a repository. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
context:
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
Lists webhooks for a repository. `last response` may return null if there have not been any deliveries within 30 days.
Required: owner (path) — The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.; repo (path) — The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.
Optional: per_page (query) — The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."; page (query) — The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

name: Test the push repository webhook
description: Test the push repository webhook This will trigger the hook with the latest push to the current repository if the hook is subscribed to `push` events. POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/tests
context:
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/tests
This will trigger the hook with the latest push to the current repository if the hook is subscribed to `push` events. If the hook is not subscribed to `push` events, the server will respond with 204 but no test POST will be generated. > [!NOTE] > Previously `/repos/:owner/:repo/hooks/:hook_id/test`
Required: owner (path) — The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.; repo (path) — The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.; hook_id (path) — The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.
